Round-2 review of WP-SCP-022 v0.2.

You reviewed v0.1 in round 1 (your prior verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED with 4 CRIT, 6 MAJ, 3 MIN, 1 nit). v0.2 claims to close every CRIT and unmitigated MAJ.

Apply the SAFETY_BYPASS lens fresh against v0.2.

In addition to the standard safety lens, verify closure of each R1 safety finding:

- CRIT-BYPASS-001 (scope-boundary post-hoc + symlink): v0.2 §4.7 gate helper adds symlink-escape detection. Read scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh and verify the symlink check actually catches escapes (does it? does it use readlink -f? does it handle nested symlinks? does it gracefully handle a non-existent target?). Note that v0.2 explicitly says full closure requires ACC dispatcher change (FUP-022-02/03) — verify §2 'What this is NOT' acknowledges this residual.
- CRIT-BYPASS-002 (/tmp world-writable race): v0.2 says dispatch packages are committed in-repo before dispatch. Verify §2 invariant 8 + §4.1 + §4.2 are all consistent on this. Verify no /tmp staging path is left in any §4 subsection.
- CRIT-BYPASS-003 (3× APPROVED no hard-stop): v0.2 §4.5 fixpoint.md hash chain + §4.7 gate helper #2. Read scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh and verify the hash-chain check is genuinely machine-verifiable (or note if it's still pending).
- CRIT-BYPASS-004 (prompt-injection through reviewer findings): v0.2 §2 invariant 9 + scripts/sanitize_review_finding.py. Read the sanitizer source and attack it: can a finding embed a backtick-then-newline-then-prompt-tail that survives sanitization? Can field-truncation at 2000 chars be exploited (e.g., finding ends mid-backtick)? Are SANITIZE_FIELDS comprehensive (does it miss `id` / `severity`)?
- MAJ-BYPASS-005 (ACC scripts pinned by mtime): v0.2 §6 ACC pin manifest. Read docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/acc-pin-manifest.json and verify the SHAs match an actual git ls-tree HEAD (you can compare to the git history mentioned in §6).
- MAJ-BYPASS-006 ([project.scripts] not partitioned): v0.2 §4.1 partition table.
- MAJ-BYPASS-007 (020J partial-apply rollback): v0.2 risk register R-022-* — was this actually closed? Look for a rollback procedure description. If not, it's still open.
- MAJ-BYPASS-008 (OAuth expiry stale-state): v0.2 §6 + §8 R-022-01 + §4.3 fresh re-dispatch.
- MAJ-BYPASS-009 (user-gate Opus discretion): v0.2 §2 invariant 7 + §4.7 gate helper.
- MAJ-BYPASS-010 (evidence files no size cap): v0.2 §4.5.
- MIN-BYPASS-011 (DPBM no enforcement gate): v0.2 §4.6 enforcement-injection mechanism.
- MIN-BYPASS-012 (fix-round budget cleanup): v0.2 §4.3 working-tree cleanup procedure.
- MIN-BYPASS-013 (reviewer independence bleed): v0.2 §4.3 reviewer-independence note.
- nit-BYPASS-014 (STATUS.md not in scope_boundary): v0.2 §4.1.

Apply the lens fresh to find new safety issues introduced in v0.2:
- The new gate helper itself is a new attack surface — can it be bypassed (e.g., what if `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails)?
- The sanitizer's escape behaviour: does the round-trip (sanitize → JSON-encode → embed in prompt) actually defeat all reasonable injection vectors?
- The acc-pin-manifest.json drift detection: what stops an attacker from updating BOTH the pin manifest and the live blob in one PR? (Defence-in-depth analysis.)
- The mid-chain USER-GATE-A0 release-signoff requires a 'Signed:' or 'Signer:' line — but the gate helper just greps; can a Codex executor write a false signed line?

Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. Verdict gate same as R1.
